Writ Petition No. 4592 of 2012
 Jitendra Verma
 Versus
 State Of M.P And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Nakul Khedkar - Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri K K Prajapati - Govt. Advocate for the respondent

Order 
With the consent of parties, the matter is heard finally.

1. The instant writ petition, filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, challenges the order dated 11.06.2012 (Annexure P/1) passed by the Adjudication Officer-cum-Additional District Magistrate under Section 51 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 whereby, the petitioner has been held guilty for selling substandard Mava and has been imposed a fine of Rs.5,00,000/-.
2.The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that at the relevant time, when the instant petition was filed, no appellate authority in terms of Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 was notified and therefore, this writ petition was filed challenging the order dated 11.06.2012 passed by the Adjudication Officer-cum-Additional District Magistrate, Morena.

He submits that subsequently vide Gazette NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27374 2 WP-4592-2012 Notification dated 30.08.2013, the concerned District Judge has been notified as the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal.

3. He further submits that since the consideration of the writ petition involves the adjudication of disputed questions of fact, he may be permitted to avail the remedy of appeal before the appellate authority.

However, he submits that while entertaining the writ petition, this Court passed a conditional interim order staying the effect and operation of the impugned order, subject to deposit of 25% of the penalty amount.
He submits that the penalty amount of Rs.1,25,000/- has been deposited by the petitioner and the stay is operating in the petition since then.
Therefore, he submits that till the adjudication of the appeal, the interim protection may be continued.

sentences.text: In view of the above, the writ petition is permitted to be withdrawn with liberty to the petitioner to avail the remedy of appeal against the order dated 11.06.2012.

In case, an appeal is preferred by the petitioner within a period of 30 days from today, the appellate authority shall consider and decide the same on merits without adverting to the question of limitation.
It is further observed that the interim relief granted to the petitioner by this Court vide order dated 12.09.2012 shall continue to remain in operation till the final disposal of the appeal.
5.With the aforesaid liberty, the petition stands disposed of as withdrawn.
6. All interlocutory applications, if any, stand closed.
